significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that, among outcome-matched scientific inputs, higher "Route-Separability Score" predicts greater within-route than cross-route transfer of route-specific activation edits; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between independently measurable quantities, alongside a form-(i) finding that route identity is represented. It establishes a substantial representational phenomenon and fixes expectations about intervention generalization, but only limited mechanism: the claim itself concedes that "Above-chance route separation does not by itself prove correct mechanistic causal use," consistent with the probing limitations surveyed by Belinkov (2022, "Probing Classifiers"). A negative result would specifically reject route separability as a diagnostic of intervention transfer, although it would not establish that models lack mechanistic knowledge because other encodings or causal pathways could remain; true and false branches are nevertheless distinguishable. In the topic-substitution check, deleting the matched-outcome routes and RSS-transfer coupling leaves only the generic question of whether scientific mechanisms are represented, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Route-Separability Score," proposed as a "read-only diagnostic" and predictor of route-specific intervention transfer rather than merely an explanatory description. It is partly ex ante: after calibration on labeled, outcome-matched examples, RSS is intended to forecast whether an intervention will generalize within versus across routes before that intervention is deployed, giving model auditors an action window. After re-extraction, the substantive prediction—higher RSS should correspond to greater "transfer-within-route minus transfer-across-route"—survives as a relation, although the explicit concession that "Findings are outcome- and model-specific" limits universal transfer; asserted scope still spans protein, molecular, and materials model classes, with scientific-model auditors and builders as the main downstream users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this reach score: the broad scientific-representation topic alone supplies neither RSS nor its forward-looking transfer prediction.
